sentences.text: Appellant has taken the ground for delay as fear of Covid-19 pandemic, which is a justifiable ground.
Considering the grounds of delay as bonafide, the application seeking condonation of delay in filing the appeal stands allowed.
The delay stands condoned.
3. Brief facts of the case are that appellant/aggrieved filed petition U/s 12 of D.V. Act impleading respondent Hem Singh Bharana, his parents and his first wife as respondents in the year 2009.
It is stated that appellant is a highly educated lady i.e. Ph.D from IIT, Delhi working in a Multi National Company in Mumbai.
It is stated in the complaint under D.V. Act that respondent is Chairman cum Managing Director in construction company namely M/s Era Construction India Ltd.

In 1992,
appellant got introduced with respondent while she was pursuing her CA NO. 102/2020 PAGE NO.
2 OF 20 Dr. RS@MB vs. HSB Purshotam Pathak studies from IIT, Delhi.
In 1993-94, she started visiting Era Construction India Ltd. of respondent.
Respondent has affluent life style at that time and he made his parents meet her parents.
Respondent represented himself to be an unmarried person and expressed his desire to marry the appellant.
Accordingly, on 13.05.1994, complainant and respondent married with each other at Qutub Hotel in presence of friends and relatives.
After their marriage, they started living together at F-1/10, Hauz Khas Enclave, New Delhi.
The marriage of the appellant and the respondent was duly consummated and they lived together as husband and wife.
After few months of marriage, respondent started abusing and physically torturing the appellant on one pretext or the other including dowry demands.
Respondent was a heavy drunkard person who tortured the appellant mentally and physically.

Appellant has cited various incidents dated 04.09.1998, 05.09.1998, 14.01.1999, 31.05.1999, 22.07.1999, 08.12.1999, 24.03.2000,
15.12.2000, 09.05.2001, alleging domestic violence and financial exploitation upon her by the respondent and his family members.
From 1998 to 2001, respondent did not give any financial assistance to the appellant rather financially exploited her by taking money from her.

Consequently,
appellant left the matrimonial home and filed complaint with CAW Cell on 01.06.2001, upon which an FIR U/s 498/406 IPC was registered against the respondent.

During investigation of said FIR, it was revealed that respondent was already married with one CA NO. 102/2020 PAGE NO. 3 OF 20 Dr. RS@MB vs. HSB Digitally signed by Purshotam Purshotam Pathak Pathak Date:
2026.02.05 16:56:56 +0530 Rekha Bharana in 1980 having two children namely Vaibhav and Ms. Rashmi from his first wife, which fact was in knowledge of parents of respondent.
Respondent introduced his children with the appellant to be children of his brother.

On the request of respondent, appellant agreed to show that these children are their children and got them admitted in Ryan International School,
Vasant Kunj wherein the name of their parents written in the admission forms as that of appellant and respondent.

It is stated that respondent developed physical relations with the appellant on the pretext of their marriage, despite respondent being already married, therefore, he is liable to be punished for offence of rape, cheating etc.
Appellant sought reliefs of protection and maintenance @ Rs. 3 lakh per month from the respondent.

Trial Court dismissed the D.V. Act complaint vide exparte impugned judgment dated 30.06.2020 with the following findings:-
"19.

Further, it is the case of the aggrieved that she learnt about the first marriage of the respondent no. 1 only in 2001 after she had filed complaints with various police authorities and the reply was received by IO during investigation.

Thus, as per her,
she lived with the CA NO. 102/2020 PAGE NO. 4 OF 20 Dr. RS@MB vs. HSB Purshotam Pathak respondent no. 1 for about 7 years and did not know the factum of his first marriage and two children for all this time.
Now, it is pertinent to note at this stage that the aggrieved in the present case is not an illiterate women, rather she is a highly educated lady and is awarded a Ph.D from IIT, Delhi.
A per her own case, she was studying at IIT at the time when she met the respondent no. 1.

Not only this, she was also visiting the office of the company where the respondent no. 1 was the Managing Director, prior to her marriage with the respondent no. 1 and continued working there even after her alleged marriage with the respondent no. 1.
Infact, she was on the Board of Directors in the company namely M/s Era Financial Services (India) Ltd. alongwith the respondent no. 1.

In my considered opinion, it is unbelievable that a highly educated lady, who is working in the same office as the man with whom she has got married, would not come to know about the first marriage and two children of the man for a period as long as 7 years.

Even if it is assumed that the parents of the respondent no. 1 and even his first wife conspired with him, it is not possible that each and every employee of the group companies of the respondent no. 1 was in conspiracy with him and deliberately concealed the factum of his first marriage and two children from the aggrieved, especially when aggrieved also represented to be the wife of the respondent no. 1 in the same office.
There cannot be such meticulous planning.

In normal course, if the second wife of the Managing Director of the Company, is also working in the same office and both of them are also on the board of directors of the same company, there is bound to be some grapevine which would ordinarily also reach the second wife.

It is beyond belief that the first wife who was still the legally wedded wife of the respondent no. 1 (and is so till date) was never mentioned in the office, that she never showed up or called at the office or that no one ever mentioned or asked about the two children of the respondent no. 1 in the office.

20. It is also unbelievable that the respondent no. 1 would have introduced his two children to the aggrieved as his nephews and his two children who would have been in the age group of 7 to 16 years from 1994 to 2001 would CA NO. 102/2020 PAGE NO. 5 OF 20 Dr. RS@MB vs. HSB Digitally signed by Purshotam Purshotam Pathak Pathak Date:
2026.02.05 16:57:08 +0530 not have objected to it or they would not have addressed the respondent no. 1 as their father.

Moreover, it is unbelievable that an educated lady like the aggrieved would agree to represent herself as the mother of nephews of her husband for the purpose of the school admissions of the children or even the Dr. Rakshita Sharma @ Meena Bharana vs Hem Singh Singh Bharana on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156552850/
3 children would agree to represent to be the children of someone else in the school.

sentences.text: Even assuming the same is true, it shows that the aggrieved was a party to making a false representation before the school.

It may also be recalled here that the aggrieved was also a party to making a false declaration in the prospectus of M/s Era Financial Services (India) Ltd.
21.
It is also pertinent to mention at this stage that admittedly in the year 2000,
petition

was filed by the aggrieved U/s 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, praying for declaration of her marriage with the respondent no. 1 as null and void on the ground that the respondent no. 1 was already married.
The said petition prima-facie shows that the aggrieved was aware about the first marriage of the respondent no. 1 prior to 2001.

In this regard, it is the case of the aggrieved that the said petition was signed by her in good faith without reading the contents thereof and her counsel had committed a fraud upon her, due to which she filed an application for withdrawal of the petition and she also filed a complaint against the said counsel.

I am, however,
not inclined to believe the said contention of the aggrieved.

Firstly, there is no such averment made by the aggrieved in her original complaint whereunder she has not even disclosed the factum of filing of the petition U/s 11 HMA in the year 2000 or the fact of filing of complaint against her counsel.

Secondly, it may be noted that aggrieved is a highly educated woman and though for once she may be believed to say that she did not read the entire contents of the petition at the time of signing,
however, it is not believable that she did not even notice that the counsel had drafted a petition for declaration of marriage as null and void U/s 11 of the HMA instead of drafting the petition for divorce U/s 13 of the HMA.
Thus, the claim of aggrieved that she was defrauded by her counsel appears to be an afterthought.

Thirdly, the documents Mark K which is purportedly a complaint filed by her against the CA NO.
102/2020 Digitally PAGE NO. 6 OF 20 Dr. RS@MB vs. HSB signed by Purshotam Purshotam Pathak Pathak Date:
2026.02.05 16:57:14 +0530 counsel who filed the petition U/s 11 HMA does not bear any acknowledgment of receipt or proof of filing and thus, the same is merely a self serving document.

22. The afore-said facts and circumstances show that the aggrieved has not disclosed true and complete facts before the court, she has herself been party to misrepresentations in the prospectus of M/s Era Financial Services (India) Ltd, the respondent no. 1 did not reside with her continuously from 1994 to 2001 in the premises at Hauz Khas Enclave and that she had access to his address where he was residing with his wife and two children and that she had filed a petition for declaration of her marriage with respondent no. 1 as null and void which was withdrawn by her on the pretest of fraud on the part of the counsel.

Thus, in my considered opinion, in view of the said facts and circumstances, it is highly improbable that the aggrieved did not have the knowledge of the first marriage of the respondent no. 1 till the year 2001 as alleged by her.

sentences.text: Furthermore, it can also not be ignored that though the aggrieved separated from the respondent no. 1 in the year 2001, present application filed by her in the year 2009 (four years after the coming into effect of the PWDV Act).
No explanation for the said delay has been given by the aggrieved in her application.

Undue and unexplained delay in filing the present case by the aggrieved who is a highly educated women and who has allegedly been defrauded, also raises doubts on the case being set up by the aggrieved.
24. From the aforesaid discussion, it is clear that the aggrieved has not approached the court with clean hands, and she has not disclosed true and complete facts in her application.
Her cause that she had no knowledge of the said facts is totally unbelievable in the facts and circumstances of the case, as discussed above.

In my opinion, the aggrieved has failed to discharge the initial burden of proof placed upon her to show that she had no knowledge of the factum of first marriage of the respondent no. 1 and it is only in 2001 that she acquired the CA NO. 102/2020 PAGE NO. 7 OF 20 Dr. RS@MB vs. HSB Digitally signed by Purshotam Purshotam Pathak Pathak Date:
2026.02.05 16:57:20 +0530 knowledge of the said fact for the first time.

Consequently, as the aggrieved chose to enter into and stay in the marital/live-in-relationship with the respondent no. 1 knowingly that he was already a married man, her relationship with the respondent no. 1 cannot be termed to be "in the nature of marriage" but the same was a adulterous and bigamous relation and it cannot be said to be "in the nature of marriage" so as to fall within the scope of 'domestic relationship' as defined in Section 2(f) of PWDV Act.

Thus, as one of the ingredients of domestic relationship between aggrieved and respondent no. 1 are not made out from the material on record, the present application filed under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the core issue involved is with regard to validity of marriage and 'domestic relationship' between the parties.

The definition of 'domestic relationship' as per Section 2 (f) of PWDV Act is as under:-
"Domestic relationship means a relationship between two CA NO. 102/2020 Digitally PAGE NO. 10 OF 20 Dr. RS@MB vs. HSB signed by Purshotam Purshotam Pathak Pathak Date:
2026.02.05 16:57:37 +0530 persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family."
10.

It is the case of the appellant/aggrieved that she was pursuaded by respondent to marry him on the assurances and representations that he was unmarried at that time and accordinlgy she married the respondent on 13.05.1994 at Qutub Hotel, Delhi and consequent thereto, they started residing together at F-1/10, Hauz Khas Enclave, New Delhi.

It is further the case of the appellant that she was subjected to mental and physical harrassment at the hands of respondent and his family members for which she has narrated specific incidents and she left the matrimonial house on 01.06.2001.

Thereafter, she lodged a complaint with CAW Cell dated 14.05.2001 and during course of investigation, it was revealed that respondent was already married to Ms. Rekha Bharana in 1980 and he is having two children born in 1985 and 1987.
It is the claim of the appellant/aggrieved that respondent concealed factum of his first marriage from her and solemonized second marriage with her.

11.It is relevant to note that it is an admitted case of the appellant that she acquired the knowledge about the first marriage of the respondent in 2001, pursuant to which she CA NO. 102/2020 Digitally signed by Purshotam PAGE NO. 11 OF 20 Dr. RS@MB vs. HSB Purshotam Pathak Pathak Date:

10.

Furthermore, appellant/aggrieved despite being a qualified lady Ph.D. from IIT, Delhi,
filed complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C. in 2008, instant D.V. Act complaint in 2009, thereby claimings incidents of domestic violence beginning from 1998 onwards i.e. 10 years after the alleged incidents.
Such a meticulous and secret arrangement and balancing of concealment about first marriage is not at all possible for the respondent to manage for a long period of 7-8 years period.
At the same time, it cannot be believed that neither the first wife nor the second wife were so diligent or conscious of movement of respondent, enabling him manage such marital relations with both.
Also, even if, it is presumed, it is not possible for the respondent to conspire with each and every person coming in contact with the appellant for alleged concealment.
At this stage, appellant/aggrieved is taking plea that though she is educated, but not legally sound and the entire burden she puts upon his counsel, which is a frivolous defence taken by her to brush aside her own wrongs.
Appellant cannot be permitted to take benefits of her own wrongs by changing her version as per her convenience.
